About this gene

Imported from the magic-gene intake, 2026-09-08. One crackle field drawn as its channels. It is the simplest gene in this batch and the clearest demonstration of what CRACKLE is for: a tiling of polygons with a genuinely hard edge, which nothing else in the vocabulary gives.

Crossing two of them

Finding one

About 1 in 893 wild horses is born showing this. That is the whole of the supply: catch one, or make one with the carrot below. Breeds set their own pools and a breed built around this gene will carry it far more often than the wild population does.

Its gene carrot

The file

common/src/main/resources/horsegenetics/genes/webbed.json — a data-driven gene, not a Java class. It is listed in the index.json beside it and registered by Genes' class initialiser at startup.

Keyhorsegenetics.webbed
Phasemagical — it adds signed colour in phase 3, after the pigment has resolved
Priority381 — where it sits in the one (priority, key) paint order
AllelesWeb · Wec · n
Varies per horse4 values drawn once off the expressing allele copy, so a foal that inherits the copy inherits the look

What it paints

Each outcome, described the way the gene file describes it, and then the layers that draw it in the order they are painted. The prose is the part a reader checks a bake against; the list underneath is what the engine actually did.

Webbed

One crackle field, drawn as its channels rather than its cells. It is the simplest gene in this family and the one that shows most clearly what CRACKLE is for: a tiling of polygons with a genuinely hard edge, which nothing else in the vocabulary can give.

  1. the venation net over the barrel and neck — CRACKLE inverted, painted with TOWARD

Webbed, coloured

The same net in a colour the line carries. Fully recessive.
